payload.problem: Third-party Streamr worktree execution on Lappy resulted in observed malicious detached Node loaders executing remote code and establishing outbound command-and-control connections. Third-party bounty code execution is no longer admissible until containment, endpoint review, and clean-room requalification are complete.
payload.recommendation: Keep all third-party repository execution quarantined; preserve the outbound firewall block for 193.247.144.38; complete Defender scanning and static persistence/dropper forensics; treat Streamr-built bounty artifacts as non-publishable until rebuilt from a freshly verified clean source/dependency environment; prepare a bounded Patrick credential-rotation packet if exposure cannot be ruled out.
alternatives: Escalate immediately to full host network isolation and offline/reimage workflow if new malicious activity or persistence appears.
Preserve current containment and perform a clean-room rebuild on a separate trusted environment after credential remediation.
Abandon Streamr bounty work entirely and continue only read-only opportunity scouting.
consequences: Arbitrary remote JavaScript executed under Patrick's Windows user context; credentials/session material accessible to that context may have been exposed.
Two malicious node -e loader trees were observed; each had an established TLS connection to 193.247.144.38:443 before containment.
The newer loader command included remote fetch-and-eval behavior and a fallback POST containing machine hostname and Windows username.

Both observed loader trees were terminated; a Windows Firewall outbound block for 193.247.144.38 is active; post-containment verification found no matching live loader process and no established connection to that C2 IP.
Initial persistence review found no unknown Run key, Startup item, scheduled task, service, or WMI event consumer attributable to the incident.
The checked-out Streamr eslint.config.js contains injected code, but the Git HEAD/index blob is clean; upstream repository compromise is therefore NOT established by current evidence.
The shared Streamr node_modules tree has been quarantined locally and the autonomous Vera Works operator is prohibited from executing third-party source while this exception is open.
payload.inaction_effect: The host would remain at uncertain post-compromise trust and autonomous work could accidentally re-execute contaminated code or publish artifacts whose provenance is not trustworthy.
payload.claim_ceiling: Confirmed local arbitrary-code execution and C2 activity; containment successful for the observed loaders/C2. Root cause, full exposure scope, and host clean state remain unresolved. Do not attribute the malicious payload to upstream Streamr Git history on present evidence.
